unit_label: Module A: International Banking - Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) and other Remittance Facilities for Residents

facts.statement: The LRS limit per financial year has been USD 25,000 from 4 February 2004, 50,000 from 20 December 2006, 1,00,000 from 8 May 2007, 2,00,000 from 26 September 2007, 75,000 from 14 August 2013, 1,25,000 from 3 June 2014 and 2,50,000 from 26 May 2015.

The USD 2,50,000 limit subsumes the current account remittances for private visits, gifts or donations, employment abroad, emigration, maintenance of relatives abroad, business trips, medical treatment and studies abroad; release beyond it requires prior permission from the Reserve Bank, except as the paragraph permits. For private visits all tour related expenses, including overseas transport, passes and hotels, are subsumed, and the tour operator may collect in rupees or foreign currency. Expenses of a business trip borne by the employer are residual current account transactions outside the LRS and may be permitted by the authorised dealer without limit after verifying bona fides.

For emigration, foreign exchange can be drawn up to the amount prescribed by the country of emigration or USD 2,50,000; any amount beyond may be allowed only for incidental expenses in the country of immigration and not for earning points or credits for immigration by investing in government bonds, land or commercial enterprises. For medical treatment authorised dealers may release up to USD 2,50,000 without an estimate; beyond that, under general permission on an estimate from a doctor in India or a hospital or doctor abroad; a person who falls sick after going abroad may also be released exchange without RBI approval, and up to USD 2,50,000 a year is allowed for an attendant accompanying a patient. For studies abroad, up to USD 2,50,000 without an estimate from the university, and above that without RBI approval on the institution's estimate.

The permissible capital account transactions of an individual under the LRS are opening a foreign currency account abroad with a bank, acquisition of immovable property abroad, overseas direct investment and overseas portfolio investment in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Rules, 2022 and its Regulations and Directions, and extending loans, including rupee loans, to NRI relatives as defined in the Companies Act, 2013.

Remittances under the scheme can be used to buy objects of art subject to other applicable law such as the Foreign Trade Policy; outward remittance may be by demand draft in the individual's own name or the beneficiary's against a self-declaration; individuals may open and hold foreign currency accounts abroad without prior RBI approval.

Authorised persons may facilitate LRS remittances to International Financial Services Centres in India for financial services or products within the IFSC, and for transactions in other jurisdictions through a foreign currency account held in an IFSC. Resident individuals may open a foreign currency account in an IFSC for these purposes and shall not settle domestic transactions with other residents through it.

The authorised dealer must ensure that payment is received out of the remitter's own funds by a cheque drawn on the applicant's account, by debit to the account, or by demand draft or pay order (or card of the cardholder); must certify that the remittance is not made directly or indirectly by or to ineligible entities; must keep on record the information on which the transaction was done; must refuse in writing and, if it suspects contravention, report to the Reserve Bank where the applicant refuses to comply; must follow KYC and anti-money laundering rules; and, for a new customer making a capital account remittance, must carry out due diligence and obtain the previous year's bank statement or the latest tax assessment order or return.

Remittances under the scheme are reported in FETERS in the normal course, and authorised dealer banks are guided by FED Master Direction No. 18/2015-16 on Reporting under FEMA, 1999. Banks, including those with no presence in India, must obtain prior RBI approval for schemes they market in India to residents for soliciting foreign currency deposits for overseas branches or acting as agents for overseas mutual funds or other foreign financial services companies.

payload.title: The LRS ceiling over the years: up, then down, then up again
payload.core_explanation_md:
The limit has moved with the macro conditions, not in a straight line.

- **4 Feb 2004**: USD 25,000 (launch)
- **20 Dec 2006**: USD 50,000
- **8 May 2007**: USD 1,00,000
- **26 Sep 2007**: USD 2,00,000 (the first peak)
- **14 Aug 2013**: cut to **USD 75,000**
- **3 Jun 2014**: raised to USD 1,25,000
- **26 May 2015**: **USD 2,50,000**, the figure that still applies

Two things to remember: the limit has **fallen once** (2013), and today's USD 2,50,000 has applied **since 26 May 2015**, the date the current account facilities were folded into it.

payload.title: Current account purposes sit inside the ceiling, with a few exits
payload.core_explanation_md:
Every current account facility an individual uses (private visits, gifts or donations, going abroad for employment, emigration, maintenance of relatives, business trips, medical treatment, studies) counts against the **same USD 2,50,000**. Beyond it, **RBI permission** is needed, except where the direction itself provides a route.

- **Private visits**: the whole trip counts, including rail or road transport, passes and overseas hotels. A tour operator may collect in rupees or foreign currency.
- **Business trips**: if the **employer** pays, the spend is a residual current account transaction **outside** the LRS, and the bank may allow it **without limit** after checking bona fides.
- **Gift or donation** and **maintenance of relatives**: up to the ceiling, with no separate sub-limit.

payload.title: The three purposes that can go beyond USD 2,50,000 without RBI
payload.core_explanation_md:
Emigration, medical care and study abroad have their own routes above the ceiling.

**Emigration**: up to the amount the destination country **prescribes**, or the ceiling. Anything more is allowed only for **incidental expenses** in the new country, never to buy eligibility through bonds, land or a business there.

**Medical treatment**: up to the ceiling **without an estimate**. Above it, the bank may release exchange under general permission on an **estimate** from a doctor in India or a hospital or doctor abroad. A person who falls ill after leaving may also be released exchange **without RBI approval**. An **attendant** accompanying the patient gets up to USD 2,50,000 a year.

**Studies**: up to the ceiling **without a university estimate**. Above it, **without RBI approval**, on the institution's estimate.

payload.title: The capital account routes, and the IFSC window
payload.core_explanation_md:
An individual may use the LRS for capital account purposes in these routes:

- opening a **foreign currency account** abroad with a bank (no prior RBI approval needed)
- buying **immovable property abroad**
- **overseas direct investment** and **overseas portfolio investment**, under the Overseas Investment Rules, Regulations and Directions of **2022**
- **loans** (including in rupees) to **NRI relatives**

Other permitted uses: **objects of art** (subject to the Foreign Trade Policy), and a **demand draft** in your own or the beneficiary's name against a self-declaration.

**IFSC window**: banks may facilitate remittances to an **International Financial Services Centre in India** for financial products there, or for transactions elsewhere through a foreign currency account held in the IFSC. You may open that account, but you may **not settle domestic transactions** with other residents through it.

payload.title: What the bank must do on every LRS remittance
payload.core_explanation_md:
The authorised dealer carries real duties.

1. **Funds**: the money must come from the **remitter's own account or instrument** (cheque on the applicant's account, debit, demand draft or pay order, or the cardholder's card).
2. **Certify** that the remittance is not made directly or indirectly **by or to ineligible entities**.
3. **Know the customer**: KYC and anti-money laundering rules apply; for a **new customer's capital account** remittance, carry out **due diligence** and get the **previous year's bank statement** or the latest tax assessment order or return.
4. **Keep records** of the information on which the transaction was done.
5. **Refuse in writing** if the applicant will not comply, and **report to RBI** if contravention or evasion is suspected.
6. **Report** the remittance through **FETERS**, following the Master Direction on reporting under FEMA.

Also: a bank may not market foreign currency deposit schemes of overseas branches, or act as agent for overseas mutual funds, in India without **prior RBI approval**.

payload.title: A fee estimate above the ceiling
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a resident student has admission abroad. The university's estimate for the first year is USD 310,000. How much can the authorised dealer remit without an estimate, how much more on the estimate, and does either part need RBI approval?

worked_steps.description: State the amount releasable without any estimate.
Subtract it from the estimate to find the part that needs the estimate.
Check whether the excess needs RBI approval.
worked_steps.formula_or_substitution: Studies abroad: above the ceiling on the institution's estimate

payload.final_answer_with_unit: USD 2,50,000 without an estimate, and the remaining USD 60,000 on the university's estimate, with no RBI approval needed for either part

self_check.prompt_text: If the same USD 60,000 were a holiday abroad instead, would the bank be able to release it?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No, not without RBI permission: the holiday sits inside the ceiling and has no exit above it.

payload.stem_md: Which statement about how the LRS limit has changed since 2004 is correct?

options.text_md: It has risen at every revision
options.explanation_md: It was reduced once, in 2013.

options.text_md: It was USD 1,00,000 when the scheme began
options.explanation_md: The scheme began at USD 25,000.

options.text_md: It was reduced to USD 75,000 in August 2013 before being raised again
options.explanation_md: The limit fell from USD 2,00,000 to USD 75,000 in 2013.

options.text_md: It has been USD 2,50,000 since 2004
options.explanation_md: USD 2,50,000 has applied since 26 May 2015.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The limit began at USD 25,000 in 2004, peaked at USD 2,00,000 in 2007, was cut to USD 75,000 in August 2013, and reached USD 2,50,000 on 26 May 2015.

payload.stem_md: A company sends its employee abroad for a conference and bears all the expenses. How is the spending treated for the employee's LRS limit?

options.text_md: It counts fully against the employee's USD 2,50,000
options.explanation_md: Expenses borne by the employer are outside the individual's LRS.

options.text_md: It is a residual current account transaction outside the LRS and may be allowed by the bank without limit, after checking bona fides
options.explanation_md: Employer-borne business trip expenses fall outside the individual's limit.

options.text_md: It needs prior RBI approval above USD 25,000
options.explanation_md: No such rule applies.

options.text_md: It is prohibited under the LRS
options.explanation_md: It is permitted; it is simply outside the LRS limit.

payload.correct_explanation_md: If the employer bears the expenses of a business trip, they are treated as residual current account transactions outside the LRS and the bank may allow them without limit after verifying bona fides.

payload.stem_md: A resident is going abroad to study and the university's estimate is above USD 2,50,000. Which statement is correct?

options.text_md: RBI approval is always needed above USD 2,50,000
options.explanation_md: For studies the bank may release more on the estimate.

options.text_md: Nothing above USD 2,50,000 can ever be remitted
options.explanation_md: The estimate route allows more.

options.text_md: The bank may release more, but only after the student has been abroad six months
options.explanation_md: No such waiting period applies.

options.text_md: The bank may remit more than USD 2,50,000 without RBI approval, based on the institution's estimate
options.explanation_md: This is the route the direction gives for studies.

payload.correct_explanation_md: For studies abroad the bank may release up to USD 2,50,000 without an estimate and more, without RBI approval, on the estimate from the institution.

payload.stem_md: A resident individual opens a foreign currency account in an IFSC under the LRS. Which of these may she NOT do through it?

options.text_md: Settle domestic transactions with another resident
options.explanation_md: Resident individuals shall not settle domestic transactions through the IFSC account.

options.text_md: Invest in financial products available in the IFSC
options.explanation_md: This is a permitted purpose.

options.text_md: Make current or capital account transactions in other jurisdictions
options.explanation_md: Permitted through a foreign currency account held in an IFSC.

options.text_md: Hold the account without prior approval for each deposit
options.explanation_md: She may open and hold the account; no approval is needed for each deposit.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Resident individuals may open a foreign currency account in an IFSC for the permitted purposes, but may not settle domestic transactions with other residents through it.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is NOT something an authorised dealer must ensure for an LRS remittance?

options.text_md: That payment comes out of the remitter's own funds by cheque, debit, demand draft or pay order
options.explanation_md: This is required.

options.text_md: That the remittance is not made directly or indirectly by or to ineligible entities, certified by the dealer
options.explanation_md: This is required.

options.text_md: That the remitter has deposited at least USD 10,000 in a foreign currency account in India
options.explanation_md: No such deposit requirement exists; banks in India cannot open foreign currency accounts for residents under the LRS.

options.text_md: That KYC and anti-money laundering rules are followed
options.explanation_md: This is required.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The dealer must ensure payment from the remitter's own funds, certify no ineligible entities are involved, and follow KYC and anti-money laundering rules; a deposit in a foreign currency account in India is not a requirement.

payload.stem_md: A resident's son is going abroad to study. The institution's estimate for the year is USD 345,500 (illustrative). The bank releases USD 2,50,000 without an estimate. How many US dollars more may the bank release on the strength of the estimate, without RBI approval?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give a whole number of US dollars.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Estimate less the amount released without an estimate: 345,500 − 250,000 = 95,500.

worked_solution_steps.description: Subtract the ceiling from the estimate.

payload.stem_md: Through which system are remittances made under the LRS reported, according to the Master Direction?

options.text_md: A daily paper return to the income-tax department
options.explanation_md: No such return is named.

options.text_md: Directly by the remitter to the RBI governor
options.explanation_md: Reporting is done by the authorised dealer.

options.text_md: Only through the annual return of the remitter
options.explanation_md: The authorised dealer reports the remittance in the normal course.

options.text_md: FETERS, with the authorised dealer guided by the Master Direction on Reporting under FEMA
options.explanation_md: This is the reporting channel the direction names.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Remittances under the scheme are reported in FETERS in the normal course, and banks follow the Master Direction on Reporting under FEMA.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is a capital account transaction permitted for an individual under the LRS?

options.text_md: Purchasing lottery tickets abroad
options.explanation_md: Lottery tickets are prohibited.

options.text_md: Acquisition of immovable property abroad
options.explanation_md: Acquisition of property abroad is a permitted capital account route.

options.text_md: Remitting margin to an overseas exchange
options.explanation_md: Margins and margin calls are not allowed.

options.text_md: Remitting funds to a person on a terrorism-risk list
options.explanation_md: Such remittances are not permitted.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Opening a foreign currency account abroad, acquiring immovable property abroad, overseas direct and portfolio investment and loans to NRI relatives are the permitted capital account routes.

payload.stem_md: Does an individual need prior RBI approval to open and hold a foreign currency account with a bank outside India for making remittances under the LRS?

options.text_md: Yes, in every case
options.explanation_md: No prior approval is needed.

options.text_md: Yes, if the balance will exceed USD 25,000
options.explanation_md: No such condition applies.

options.text_md: No, prior approval is not needed
options.explanation_md: The Master Direction allows it without prior approval.

options.text_md: Yes, but only for the first account
options.explanation_md: No approval is needed for any such account.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Individuals can open, maintain and hold foreign currency accounts with a bank outside India for remittances under the scheme without prior approval of the Reserve Bank.
